correctness.rationale: The finite product kernel decomposes at coordinate i as A+Bχ_i(x_i)χ_i(Y_i). The common-value product has mean zero in [-1,1/ρ_i], while the rare-value product is the mean-zero two-point extremal law supported on [-1,ρ_i]. Chord/Jensen domination for every real convex function of a complex affine image proves the all-coefficient rare-row ordering. Equality of L1/L∞ norms follows from algebraic symmetry K(x,y)=K(y,x). The degree-at-most-two binomial formula follows from elementary symmetric identities, and the Gaussian fixed-bias limit uses CLT/LLN plus uniform fourth-moment bounds. Replayed exact finite checker: 60 spectra, 744 rows, 65 quadratic parameters and 60 monotonicity instances; finite checks do not establish the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The theorem provides a single fixed common maximizing row for the entire 2^n-coefficient complex Fourier multiplier algebra of a nonhomogeneous product measure. It avoids a row optimization over 2^n evaluations for all masks and yields an additional convex-order theorem and sharp bias-balancing monotonicity. This is a structural extension substantially beyond a single affine projector and gives exact sharp stability constants for nonlinear Fourier filters; the quadratic Gaussian coefficient is a motivated illustration rather than the sole contribution.
